cohort: The study included 782 patients who underwent IVF-ET/FET treatment and were diagnosed with clinical pregnancy, divided into a SCH group (n=256) and a control group (n=526).
finding: A nomogram successfully predicted the occurrence of SCH based on risk factors including fresh embryo transfer, polycystic ovary syndrome, hydrosalpinx, and thin endometrium, and the incidence of miscarriage was found to be higher in patients with SCH.
mod_finding: The occurrence of subchorionic hematoma (SCH) did not influence the mode of delivery for patients with successful deliveries.
